summary: A critique of journalist Michael Lewis and Going Infinite, his sympathetic 2023 book on FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried, set against trial evidence of the fraud and Lewis's earlier uncritical portraits of his subjects.

evidence.note: host says most of the story is a critique of Michael Lewis rather than SBF
Lewis arranges to shadow SBF in the Bahamas in early 2022
Lewis biography begins with his 1960 New Orleans birth and elite upbringing
long segment on The Blind Side, the left tackle and Michael Oher's football career
critique of how the book sidelines Oher's voice; his 2023 conservatorship lawsuit
close reading of Going Infinite begins and runs through most of part two
John Ray's account of FTX's missing record keeping versus Lewis's portrayal
customer dollar deposits routed into Alameda, a point the book downplays
late-2023 trial testimony compared with Lewis's version of events

notes: Format is a judgement call: roughly two thirds is a close review of Going Infinite, plus a Lewis biography and current-affairs material on the 2023 trial. Precedence gives media-reading. SBF is listed as a third primary as the story's acknowledged bastard. Caroline Ellison, John Ray and Michael Oher kept to keywords to stay within five subjects.
